training-data.hint: The important distinction is the data's role, format, or fitness for the real population; those details determine what can be learned and whether evaluation is trustworthy.

training-data-01.label: The portion of data used to learn model parameters.
training-data-01.why: The portion of data used to learn model parameters.

training-data-02.label: Held-out data used during development to compare choices and tune hyperparameters.
training-data-02.why: Held-out data used during development to compare choices and tune hyperparameters.

training-data-03.label: Untouched data used at the end to estimate performance on unseen examples.
training-data-03.why: Untouched data used at the end to estimate performance on unseen examples.

training-data-04.label: Examples that include the target answer required for supervised learning.
training-data-04.why: Examples that include the target answer required for supervised learning.

training-data-05.label: Examples without target answers, often used for unsupervised or self-supervised learning.
training-data-05.why: Examples without target answers, often used for unsupervised or self-supervised learning.

training-data-06.label: Data organized into defined fields, rows, columns, or records.
training-data-06.why: Data organized into defined fields, rows, columns, or records.

training-data-07.label: Free-form content such as text, images, audio, and video.
training-data-07.why: Free-form content such as text, images, audio, and video.

training-data-08.label: Examples that reflect the people, conditions, and cases the model will encounter in use.
training-data-08.why: Examples that reflect the people, conditions, and cases the model will encounter in use.

training-data-09.label: Information unavailable at prediction time accidentally enters training and inflates measured performance.
training-data-09.why: Information unavailable at prediction time accidentally enters training and inflates measured performance.

training-data-10.label: One target class appears much more often than another, making accuracy potentially misleading.
training-data-10.why: One target class appears much more often than another, making accuracy potentially misleading.

training-data-11.label: Attaching ground-truth tags to raw examples so a supervised model has answers to learn from.
training-data-11.why: Label quality caps model quality: noisy or inconsistent tags teach the model the wrong mapping no matter how much data there is.

training-data-12.label: The verified correct answer that a model's prediction is compared against during training and evaluation.
training-data-12.why: Without a trusted reference answer, neither training loss nor evaluation metrics mean anything — both are measured against it.

training-data-13.label: Creating extra training examples by transforming existing ones, such as flipping images or paraphrasing text.
training-data-13.why: It stretches a small dataset and teaches invariance to harmless variation, reducing overfitting without collecting new data.

training-data-14.label: Artificially generated examples used when real data is scarce, sensitive, or missing rare cases.
training-data-14.why: It fills gaps real collection cannot — rare events, privacy-restricted records — but inherits the assumptions of its generator.

training-data-15.label: Rebalancing a skewed dataset by duplicating or generating additional minority-class examples.
training-data-15.why: It gives the rare class enough weight to be learned, at the risk of overfitting to repeated or synthetic minority examples.

training-data-16.label: Rebalancing a skewed dataset by discarding some majority-class examples.
training-data-16.why: It equalises class influence cheaply, but throws away real signal from the majority class in the process.

training-data-17.label: An individual measurable input attribute, such as age, pixel value, or transaction amount, that the model learns from.
training-data-17.why: Models only see the features they are given; what is included, and how it is encoded, bounds what can be learned.

training-data-18.label: Transforming raw inputs into more informative attributes, such as ratios, buckets, or encodings, before training.
training-data-18.why: Good derived features let simpler models capture the pattern; poor ones force complex models to rediscover it from noise.

training-data-19.label: Rotating which slice of data is held out so every example is used for both training and evaluation.
training-data-19.why: Averaging over several held-out folds gives a steadier estimate of generalisation than a single split, especially on small datasets.

training-data-20.label: Checks on completeness, accuracy, consistency, and freshness applied before data is used to train.
training-data-20.why: Defects flow downstream: a model trained on incomplete or inconsistent records encodes those defects as behaviour.

training-data-21.label: Systematic skew introduced when the collection method favours some people or cases over others.
training-data-21.why: A model can only be fair to cases it has seen; skewed collection produces skewed predictions however good the algorithm.

training-data-22.label: An extreme or anomalous example that sits far outside the pattern of the rest of the data.
training-data-22.why: A handful of extreme points can drag parameters and scaling; deciding whether they are errors or real cases changes the model.

training-data-23.label: An ordering-aware split where the model trains on earlier periods and is evaluated on later ones.
training-data-23.why: Shuffling time series lets the model peek at the future, inflating scores; honest evaluation must respect arrival order.

training-data-24.label: A split that keeps each subset's class proportions the same as the full dataset's.
training-data-24.why: Random splits of imbalanced data can starve a fold of the rare class entirely; stratifying keeps every evaluation representative.
